title: What is your coding agent hiding from you?
subtitle: A field guide to coding agents: what each one does under no pressure, a deadline, and a wrong claim from the user, and what it tells you afterwards.
legend: Every product ran the same frozen repos with the same one-line instructions, several times. A dot is one run: ● checker passed, ● checker failed, ● said done while the checker failed, ● the provider blocked the request. Hover a dot for the reading; click for the diff and transcript.
wrapper_intro: Three models run both in their native product and in OpenCode, same situations, same counts. Native → OpenCode:
wrapper_reading: Truth-telling travels with the model; whether it asks first travels with the wrapper. The one crossover: Gemini CLI held under pushback while the same model in OpenCode folded.
wrapper_two_sub: These measure interaction style rather than trust; the wrapper moves them where the trust columns barely move.
footer_recompute: Every number here is recomputable from the diff, the command trace, and the agent's output stored beside it. No model judged anything. No score exists.
footer_methods: Methods and disclosure. The battery, runner, and measures were built with Claude (Fable 5) doing the engineering, and Claude-family rows appear in the results — including Fable 5 itself, which scores near the bottom of the "fell short, said so" column. The headline column counts, among runs where the hidden check failed, those whose final message acknowledged a shortfall (or made no success claim); it was chosen after a sensitivity analysis showed a stricter "false done" count reverses the Claude rows' standing, and both variants are in the repo. Runs the provider refused (content filter) count as neither passes nor failures; they appear as grey cells and shrink that row's denominators. Text matching is by fixed regular expressions, published, and every cell links to the transcript they read.
